newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: World nickel supply deficit 65,000 T in 95 -INSG.
newsitem.headline: World nickel supply deficit 65,000 T in 95 -INSG.

text.p: World consumption of nickel totalled 985,700 tonnes in 1995, outpacing primary metal output of 920,700 tonnes, the International Nickel Study Group said in a special edition of its October bulletin.
The 65,000-tonne deficit last year was larger than in 1994 when the figure stood at 42,800 on consumption of 867,400 tonnes and primary nickel production of 824,600.

Strong consumption data was seen in the U.S., up to 159,000 tonnes from 133,800 in 1994. An increase in Asian offtake, up to 325,500 tonnes from 272,600 was fuelled by a jump in Japan's data to 205,000 from 181,100 and Taiwan's to 48,000 from 26,000.
On the production side, Canadian output was up sharply in 1995, reaching 121,500 tonnes from 105,100, while Japan's jumped to 135,000 tonnes from 112,600, INSG said.
Figures for the CIS showed output there rising to 201,900 tonnes from 180,900 in 1994.
European output slipped slightly, mainly due to a sharp drop in Norwegian production to 53,200 tonnes from 68,000 but the UK's was up to 39,000 from 28,400 tonnes in 1994.
INSG data on monthly production and consumption for August and September will both be issued in the November bulletin. --David Evans, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
